Changed after the price check: frozen FLORETS are £1.50/kg, cheaper than whole heads at £1.19 each, and they skip the worst twenty minutes of Sunday. Blitz them from frozen, in two batches on the two Sundays. Do NOT buy ready-riced — that is £4.83/kg.

THE BIG ONE. 2.4 kg across the fortnight and bagged spinach is dead in four days. Every single use in both weeks is wilted or cooked — not one is raw. Buy it all frozen. It is cheaper, it is already blanched, and nothing about the plan changes.
Borderline — fresh would just about last Week A. But both uses are steamed, so frozen costs nothing and removes a top-up line.
Frozen sliced okra is standard and often better — it's picked and frozen young. Straight from the bag into the pot, no defrosting.

2.4 kg, and the largest single top-up line. Keep them out of the fridge — cold kills the flavour and doesn't extend the life much.
1.68 kg. Buy four 500 g cartons rather than two big ones — an opened carton is five days, and this is spread across eight different dishes.

Whole heads, not bagged leaves. Bagged salad is four days; a whole gem is ten.

Buy a whole cabbage, not a shredded bag. It is the best keeper in the fridge and half the price.
